Foreword前言

The field of artificial intelligence is at a fascinating inflection point. We are moving beyond building models that can simply process information to creating intelligent systems that can reason, plan, and act to achieve complex goals with ambiguous tasks. These “agentic” systems, as this book so aptly describes them, represent the next frontier in AI, and their development is a challenge that excites and inspires us at Google.

人工智能领域正处在一个令人着迷的转折点上。我们正在超越“只能处理信息”的模型，迈向能够推理、规划并采取行动、从而在模糊任务中实现复杂目标的智能系统。正如本书恰如其分地描述的那样，这些“智能体式”（agentic）系统代表着 AI 的下一个前沿，而它们的研发，正是一项让我们 Google 人既兴奋又备受鼓舞的挑战。

Agentic Design Patterns: A Hands-On Guide to Building Intelligent Systems arrives at the perfect moment to guide us on this journey. The book rightly points out that the power of large language models, the cognitive engines of these agents, must be harnessed with structure and thoughtful design. Just as design patterns revolutionized software engineering by providing a common language and reusable solutions to common problems, the agentic patterns in this book will be foundational for building robust, scalable, and reliable intelligent systems.

《Agentic Design Patterns: A Hands-On Guide to Building Intelligent Systems》（智能体设计模式：构建智能系统实践指南）恰在此时问世，为我们指引这段旅程。本书正确地指出：大语言模型作为这些智能体的认知引擎，其威力必须通过结构化、深思熟虑的设计才能被驾驭。正如设计模式曾以一套共同语言和针对常见问题的可复用解决方案革新了软件工程，本书中的智能体模式，也将成为构建健壮、可扩展、可靠的智能系统的基石。

The metaphor of a “canvas” for building agentic systems is one that resonates deeply with our work on Google’s Vertex AI platform. We strive to provide developers with the most powerful and flexible canvas on which to build the next generation of AI applications. This book provides the practical, hands-on guidance that will empower developers to use that canvas to its full potential. By exploring patterns from prompt chaining and tool use to agent-to-agent collaboration, self-correction, safety, and guardrails, this book offers a comprehensive toolkit for any developer looking to build sophisticated AI agents.

把构建智能体系统比作一块“画布”，这一比喻与我们在 Google Vertex AI 平台上的工作深深共鸣。我们努力为开发者提供最强大、最灵活的画布，让他们在其上构建下一代 AI 应用。本书则提供了务实、动手的指导，赋能开发者把这块画布用到极致。从提示链、工具调用，到智能体间协作、自我纠错、安全与护栏，本书探索了一系列模式，为任何希望构建复杂 AI 智能体的开发者提供了一套完整工具箱。

The future of AI will be defined by the creativity and ingenuity of developers who can build these intelligent systems. Agentic Design Patterns is an indispensable resource that will help to unlock that creativity. It provides the

AI 的未来，将由那些能够构建这些智能系统的开发者的创造力与巧思来定义。《Agentic Design Patterns》是一份不可或缺的资源，将助力释放这种创造力。它提供了

essential knowledge and practical examples to understand not only the “what” and “why” of agentic systems, but also the “how.”

必备的知识与实践示例，让你不仅理解智能体系统的“是什么”和“为什么”，更懂得“怎么做”。

I am thrilled to see this book in the hands of the developer community. The patterns and principles within these pages will undoubtedly accelerate the development of innovative and impactful AI applications that will shape our world for years to come.

看到这本书交到开发者社区手中，我由衷地高兴。书中的模式与原则，必将加速那些富有创新性、具有影响力的 AI 应用的开发，而这些应用将在未来岁月里塑造我们的世界。

A Thought Leader’s Perspective: Power and Responsibility一位思想领袖的视角：力量与责任

Of all the technology cycles I have witnessed over the past four decades—from the birth of the personal computer and the web to the revolutions in mobile and cloud—none has felt quite like this one. For years, the discourse around artificial intelligence was a familiar rhythm of hype and disillusionment, the so-called AI summers followed by long, cold winters. But this time, something is different. The conversation has palpably shifted. If the last 18 months were about the engine—the breathtaking, almost vertical ascent of large language models (LLMs)—the next era will be about the car we build around it. It will be about the frameworks that harness this raw power, transforming it from a generator of plausible text into a true agent of action.

在过去四十年里我亲历过的所有技术周期中——从个人电脑和互联网的诞生，到移动与云的革命——没有哪一次像这一次。多年来，围绕人工智能的话语总是熟悉的一套节奏：炒作与幻灭交替，所谓的“AI 夏天”之后便是漫长寒冷的冬天。但这一次，有些东西不一样了。对话实实在在地发生了转变。如果说过去 18 个月属于引擎——大语言模型（LLM）那令人屏息、近乎垂直的跃升——那么下一个时代将属于我们围绕这台引擎打造的那辆车。它将属于那些驾驭这种原始力量的框架，把它从一个“貌似合理的文本生成器——转变为一个真正能够行动的智能体。

I admit that I began as a skeptic. Plausibility, I have found, is often inversely proportional to one’s own knowledge of a subject. Early models, for all their fluency, felt like they were operating with a kind of impostor syndrome, optimized for credibility over correctness. But then came the inflection point, a step change brought about by a new class of “reasoning” models. Suddenly, we were not just conversing with a statistical machine that predicted the next word in a sequence; we were getting a peek into a nascent form of cognition.

我承认，自己一开始是个怀疑者。我发现，一段话语的“貌似合理”，往往与说话者对该主题的实际了解成反比。早期模型尽管流利，却给人一种带着“冒名顶替综合征”运行的感觉——被优化得更像可信，而不是正确。但随后拐点来了，一类全新的“推理”模型带来了阶跃式变化。突然间，我们不再只是和一台预测序列中下一个词的统计机器对话；我们得以窥见一种萌芽状态的认知。

The first time I experimented with one of the new agentic coding tools, I felt that familiar spark of magic. I tasked it with a personal project I had never found the time for: migrating a charity website from a simple web builder to a proper, modern CI/CD environment. For the next 20 min, it went to work, asking clarifying questions, requesting credentials, and providing status updates. It felt less like using a tool and more like collaborating with a junior developer. When it presented me with a fully deployable package, complete with impeccable documentation and unit tests, I was floored.

当我第一次试用新的智能体式编码工具时，我感受到了那种熟悉的魔法火花。我交给它一个我一直没空做的个人项目：把一个慈善机构网站从简单的建站工具迁移到一套像样的、现代的 CI/CD 环境。接下来的 20 分钟里，它埋头干活，提出澄清性问题、申请凭证、并汇报进展。那感觉不像是在用一个工具，更像是在和一位初级开发者协作。当它交给我一个完全可部署的包、还附带无可挑剔的文档和单元测试时，我彻底折服了。

— 原书第 8 页 —

Of course, it was not perfect. It made mistakes. It got stuck. It required my supervision and, crucially, my judgment to steer it back on course. The experience drove home a lesson I have learned the hard way over a long career: you cannot afford to trust blindly. Yet, the process was fascinating. Peeking into its “chain of thought” was like watching a mind at work: messy, nonlinear, full of starts, stops, and self-corrections, not unlike our own human reasoning. It was not a straight line; it was a random walk towards a solution. Here was the kernel of something new: not just an intelligence that could generate content, but also one that could generate a plan.

当然，它并不完美。它会犯错，会卡住，需要我监督，更关键的是需要我的判断力把它扳回正轨。这次经历让我再次深刻体会到漫长职业生涯里换来的一条教训：你承担不起盲目信任的代价。然而，这个过程又令人着迷。偷看它的“思维链”，就像在观察一个大脑运转：杂乱、非线性、充满开始、停顿和自我纠正，和我们人类自己的推理没什么两样。它不是一条直线，而是一场朝向解的随机游走。这里蕴含着某种新东西的内核：一种不仅能生成内容、还能生成计划的智能。

This is the promise of agentic frameworks. It is the difference between a static subway map and a dynamic GPS that reroutes you in real time. A classic rule-based automaton follows a fixed path; when it encounters an unexpected obstacle, it breaks. An AI agent, powered by a reasoning model, has the potential to observe, adapt, and find another way. It possesses a form of digital common sense that allows it to navigate the countless edge cases of reality. It represents a shift from simply telling a computer what to do to explaining why we need something done and trusting it to figure out the how.

这正是智能体框架的承诺。它就像一张静态地铁图与一台实时为你重新规划路线的动态 GPS 之间的差别。经典的基于规则的自动机沿固定路径运行；一旦遇到意料之外的障碍，它就崩溃。而一个由推理模型驱动的 AI 智能体，则有能力观察、适应、另辟蹊径。它具备一种数字版的常识，足以应付现实中无穷无尽的边缘情况。它代表着一种转变：从简单地告诉计算机“做什么”，转变为向它解释“为什么要做”，并信任它自己去琢磨“怎么做”。

As exhilarating as this new frontier is, it brings a profound sense of responsibility, particularly from my vantage point as the CIO of a global financial institution. The stakes are immeasurably high. An agent that makes a mistake while creating a recipe for a “chicken salmon fusion pie” is a fun anecdote. An agent that makes a mistake while executing a trade, managing risk, or handling client data is a real problem. I have read the disclaimers and the cautionary tales: the web automation agent that, after failing a login, decided to email a member of parliament to complain about login walls. It is a darkly humorous reminder that we are dealing with a technology we do not fully understand.

尽管这一新 frontier 令人振奋，它也带来了沉甸甸的责任感——尤其是站在我这样一家全球金融机构 CIO 的位置上。利害关系高得无法估量。一个智能体在编造“鸡肉三文鱼融合派”食谱时出了错，不过是一桩趣闻轶事；而一个智能体在执行交易、管理风险或处理客户数据时出了错，就是真问题了。我读过那些免责声明和警示故事：那个网页自动化智能体在登录失败后，竟然决定给一位议员发邮件投诉登录墙。它带着一丝黑色幽默地提醒我们：我们正在应对一项自己尚未完全理解的技术。

This is where craft, culture, and a relentless focus on our principles become our essential guide. Our engineering tenets are not just words on a page; they are our compass. We must Build with Purpose, ensuring that every agent we design starts from a clear understanding of the client problem we are solving. We must Look Around Corners, anticipating failure modes and designing systems that are resilient by design. And above all, we must Inspire Trust, by being transparent about our methods and accountable for our outcomes.

正是在这里，匠心、文化以及对原则的不懈坚持，成了我们不可或缺的指南。我们的工程信条不只是纸上的字句，它们是我们的罗盘。我们必须“带着目标去构建”（Build with Purpose），确保我们设计的每一个智能体，都从对所解决客户问题的清晰理解出发。我们必须“环视拐角”（Look Around Corners），预判失败模式，从设计上就让系统具备韧性。而最重要的是，我们必须“激发信任”（Inspire Trust），对我们的方法保持透明，对我们的结果负责。

In an agentic world, these tenets take on new urgency. The hard truth is that you cannot simply overlay these powerful new tools onto messy, inconsistent systems and expect good results. Messy systems plus agents are a recipe for disaster. An AI trained on “garbage” data does not just produce garbage-out; it produces plausible, confident garbage that can poison an entire process. Therefore, our first and most critical task is to prepare the ground. We must invest in clean data, consistent metadata, and well-defined APIs. We

在智能体世界里，这些信条有了新的紧迫性。残酷的现实是：你不能简单地把这些强大的新工具叠加到杂乱、不一致的旧系统上，还指望得到好结果。杂乱系统加智能体，是一剂灾难的配方。一个用“垃圾”数据训练出来的 AI，不只是“垃圾进、垃圾出”；它产出的是貌似合理、自信满满的垃圾，足以毒化整个流程。因此，我们首要、也是最关键的任务，是把地基打好。我们必须投资于干净的数据、一致的元数据和定义良好的 API。我们

— 原书第 9 页 —

have to build the modern “interstate system” that allows these agents to operate safely and at high velocity. It is the hard, foundational work of building a programmable enterprise, an “enterprise as software,” where our processes are as well architected as our code.

还必须修建现代版的“州际公路系统”，让这些智能体能够安全、高速地运行。这是一项艰苦的奠基工作：打造一个可编程的企业、一个“即软件的企业”（enterprise as software），让我们的流程像代码一样架构精良。

Ultimately, this journey is not about replacing human ingenuity, but about augmenting it. It demands a new set of skills from all of us: the ability to explain a task with clarity, the wisdom to delegate, and the diligence to verify the quality of the output. It requires us to be humble, to acknowledge what we do not know, and to never stop learning. The pages that follow in this book offer a technical map for building these new frameworks. My hope is that you will use them not just to build what is possible, but also to build what is right, what is robust, and what is responsible.

归根结底，这段旅程不是要取代人类的聪明才智，而是要增强它。它要求我们所有人具备一套新技能：清晰解释任务的能力、知人善任的智慧，以及核验输出质量的勤勉。它要求我们保持谦逊，承认自己的无知，并永不停止学习。本书接下来的篇章，为构建这些新框架提供了一份技术地图。我的希望是：你不仅用它去构建“可行”的东西，更用它去构建“正当”、“健壮”和“负责任”的东西。

The world is asking every engineer to step up. I am confident that we are ready for the challenge.

这个世界正在呼唤每一位工程师站出来。我相信，我们已准备好迎接挑战。

Enjoy the journey.

愿你享受这段旅程。

CIO, Engineering, Goldman Sachs · Marco Argenti · New York, NY, USA

Prologue序言

What Makes an AI System an Agent?是什么让一个 AI 系统成为智能体？

  1. 1. Get the mission: You give it a goal, like “organize my schedule.”1. 明确任务：你给它一个目标，比如“帮我安排日程”。
  2. 2. Scan the scene: It gathers all the necessary information—reading emails, checking calendars, and accessing contacts—to understand what is happening.2. 勘察现场：它收集所有必要信息——读邮件、查日历、访问联系人——以了解正在发生什么。
  3. 3. Think it through: It devises a plan of action by considering the optimal approach to achieve the goal.3. 通盘思考：它通过考量实现目标的最佳路径，制定出一份行动计划。
  4. 4. Take action: It executes the plan by sending invitations, scheduling meetings, and updating your calendar.4. 采取行动：它执行计划——发送邀请、安排会议、更新你的日历。
  5. 5. Learn and get better: It observes successful outcomes and adapts accordingly. For example, if a meeting is rescheduled, the system learns from this event to enhance its future performance.5. 学习并改进：它观察成功的结果并据此调整。例如，如果一次会议被改期，系统会从这件事中学习，以提升未来的表现。

Agents are becoming increasingly popular at a stunning pace. According to recent studies, a majority of large IT companies are actively using these agents, and a fifth of them just started within the past year. The financial markets are also taking notice. By the end of 2024, AI agent startups had raised more than $2 billion, and the market was valued at $5.2 billion. It is expected to explode

智能体正以惊人的速度变得越来越普及。近期研究表明，大多数大型 IT 公司都在积极使用这些智能体，其中五分之一是在过去一年里才刚刚起步的。金融市场也注意到了这一点。到 2024 年底，AI 智能体初创公司已融资超过 20 亿美元，市场规模估值达 52 亿美元。预计它将爆发式

— 原书第 11 页 —

to nearly $200 billion in value by 2034. In short, all signs point to AI agents playing a massive role in our future economy.

增长，到 2034 年市值逼近 2000 亿美元。简言之，所有迹象都表明：AI 智能体将在我们未来的经济中扮演举足轻重的角色。

The intent of this book is to discuss the design patterns of how specialized agents can work in concert and collaborate to achieve complex goals, and you will see one paradigm of collaboration and interaction in each chapter.

本书的意图，是讨论那些专门化的智能体如何协同工作、协作以达成复杂目标的设计模式；在每一章里，你都会看到一种协作与交互的范式。

Level 0: The Core Reasoning EngineLevel 0：核心推理引擎

While an LLM is not an agent in itself, it can serve as the reasoning core of a basic agentic system. In a “Level 0” configuration, the LLM operates without tools, memory, or environment interaction, responding solely based on its

尽管 LLM 本身还不是一个智能体，但它可以充当一个基础智能体系统的推理内核。在“Level 0”配置下，LLM 不使用工具、没有记忆、也不与环境交互，仅仅基于自身的

— 原书第 12 页 —
— 原书第 13 页 —

pretrained knowledge. Its strength lies in leveraging its extensive training data to explain established concepts. The trade-off for this powerful internal reasoning is a complete lack of current-event awareness. For instance, it would be unable to name the 2025 Oscar winner for “Best Picture” if that information is outside its pretrained knowledge.

预训练知识来作答。它的长处在于利用海量训练数据去解释已有的概念。这种强大内部推理能力的代价，是完全缺乏对时事的感知。例如，如果 2025 年奥斯卡“最佳影片”得主这一信息不在其预训练知识之内，它就答不上来。

Level 1: The Connected Problem-SolverLevel 1：联网的问题求解者

At this level, the LLM becomes a functional agent by connecting to and utilizing external tools. Its problem-solving is no longer limited to its pretrained knowledge. Instead, it can execute a sequence of actions to gather and process information from sources like the Internet (via search) or databases (via retrieval-augmented generation or RAG). For detailed information, refer to Chap. 14.

在这一层，LLM 通过连接并使用外部工具，成为一个真正能干活的智能体。它的问题求解不再局限于预训练知识；相反，它可以执行一连串动作，从互联网（经搜索）或数据库（经检索增强生成，即 RAG）等来源收集并处理信息。详见第 14 章。

For instance, to find new TV shows, the agent recognizes the need for current information, uses a search tool to find it, and then synthesizes the results. Crucially, it can also use specialized tools for higher accuracy, such as calling a financial API to get the live stock price for AAPL. This ability to interact with the outside world across multiple steps is the core capability of a Level 1 agent.

例如，要找新出的电视剧，智能体会意识到需要最新信息，于是使用搜索工具去查找，再对结果进行综合。关键在于，它还能使用专门工具以获得更高准确率，比如调用金融 API 获取 AAPL 的实时股价。这种跨多个步骤与外部世界交互的能力，正是 Level 1 智能体的核心能力。

Level 2: The Strategic Problem-SolverLevel 2：战略性问题求解者

At this level, an agent’s capabilities expand significantly, encompassing strategic planning, proactive assistance, and self-improvement, with prompt engineering and context engineering as core enabling skills.

在这一层，智能体的能力大幅扩展，涵盖战略规划、主动协助与自我改进，而提示工程（prompt engineering）与上下文工程（context engineering）是其核心赋能技能。

First, the agent moves beyond single-tool use to tackle complex, multipart problems through strategic problem-solving. As it executes a sequence of actions, it actively performs context engineering: the strategic process of selecting, packaging, and managing the most relevant information for each step. For example, to find a coffee shop between two locations, it first uses a mapping tool. It then engineers this output, curating a short, focused context—perhaps just a list of street names—to feed into a local search tool, preventing cognitive overload and ensuring that the second step is efficient and accurate. To achieve maximum accuracy from an AI, it must be given a short, focused, and powerful context. Context engineering is the discipline that accomplishes this by strategically selecting, packaging, and managing the most critical information from all available sources. It effectively curates the model’s limited attention to prevent overload and ensure high-quality,

首先，智能体超越了单一工具的使用，通过战略性问题求解来处理复杂的、多部分的问题。在执行一连串动作时，它会主动进行上下文工程：为每一步策略性地选择、打包并管理最相关信息的过程。例如，要在两个地点之间找一家咖啡馆，它先用地图工具；接着对输出进行“工程化”整理，裁剪出一段简短而聚焦的上下文——也许只是一串街道名——再喂给本地搜索工具，从而避免认知过载，确保第二步高效而准确。要让 AI 发挥最高准确率，就必须给它一段简短、聚焦而有力的上下文。上下文工程正是这样一门学科：它策略性地从所有可用来源中选择、打包并管理最关键的信息，有效调度模型有限的注意力，防止过载，确保在任意给定任务上都能高质量、

— 原书第 14 页 —

efficient performance. For detailed information, refer to Chap. 22.

高效地表现。详见第 22 章。

This level leads to proactive and continuous operation. A travel assistant linked to your email demonstrates this by engineering the context from a verbose flight confirmation email; it selects only the key details (flight numbers, dates, locations) to package for subsequent tool calls to your calendar and a weather API.

这一层带来了主动、持续的运作方式。一个与你邮箱相连的旅行助手就是例证：它从一封冗长的航班确认邮件中工程化地整理上下文，只挑选关键细节（航班号、日期、地点）打包，供后续调用日历和天气 API 时使用。

In specialized fields like software engineering, the agent manages an entire workflow by applying this discipline. When assigned a bug report, it reads the report, accesses the codebase, and then strategically engineers these large sources of information into a potent, focused context that allows it to efficiently write, test, and submit the correct code patch.

在软件工程这样的专业领域，智能体通过践行这门纪律来管理整条工作流。当拿到一份 bug 报告时，它阅读报告、访问代码库，然后策略性地把这些庞杂的信息源工程化地整理成一段有力、聚焦的上下文，从而高效地写出、测试并提交正确的代码补丁。

Finally, the agent achieves self-improvement by refining its own context engineering processes. When it asks for feedback on how a prompt could have been improved, it is learning how to better curate its initial inputs. This allows it to automatically improve how it packages information for future tasks, creating a powerful, automated feedback loop that increases its accuracy and efficiency over time. For detailed information, refer to Chap. 17.

最后，智能体通过精修自身的上下文工程流程来实现自我改进。当它请求反馈、询问某条提示词本可以如何改进时，它就是在学习如何更好地策划自己的初始输入。这让它能够自动改进自己为未来任务打包信息的方式，形成一条强大的自动化反馈回路，随时间推移不断提升准确率与效率。详见第 17 章。

Level 3: The Rise of Collaborative Multi-Agent SystemsLevel 3：协作式多智能体系统的兴起

At Level 3, we see a significant paradigm shift in AI development, moving away from the pursuit of a single, all-powerful superagent towards the rise of sophisticated, collaborative multi-agent systems. In essence, this approach recognizes that complex challenges are often best solved not by a single generalist, but by a team of specialists working in concert. This model directly mirrors the structure of a human organization, where different departments are assigned specific roles and collaborate to tackle multifaceted objectives. The collective strength of such a system lies in this division of labor and the synergy created through coordinated effort. For detailed information, refer to Chap. 7.

在 Level 3，我们看到 AI 开发出现了一次重大范式转变：从追求一个无所不能的单一超级智能体，转向复杂、协作式多智能体系统的兴起。本质上，这种思路认识到：复杂挑战往往不是由一个通才解决得最好，而是由一队协同工作的专家解决得最好。这一模型直接映射了人类组织的结构——不同部门被指派不同角色，协作应对多面性目标。这种系统的集体力量，正来自这种分工以及协同努力所创造的协同效应。详见第 7 章。

To bring this concept to life, consider the intricate workflow of launching a new product. Rather than one agent attempting to handle every aspect, a “Project Manager” agent could serve as the central coordinator. This manager would orchestrate the entire process by delegating tasks to other specialized agents: a “Market Research” agent to gather consumer data, a “Product Design” agent to develop concepts, and a “Marketing” agent to craft promotional materials. The key to their success would be seamless communication and information sharing between them, ensuring that all individual efforts align to achieve the collective goal.

为了让这个概念落地，不妨设想发布一款新产品这条错综复杂的工作流。不是由一个智能体试图包揽方方面面，而是由一个“项目经理”智能体担任中央协调者。这位经理通过把任务委派给其他专门智能体来编排整个流程：一个“市场调研”智能体收集消费者数据，一个“产品设计”智能体开发概念，一个“市场营销”智能体制作推广物料。它们成功的关键，在于彼此之间无缝的通信与信息共享，确保所有个体的努力都对齐于共同的目标。

— 原书第 15 页 —

While this vision of autonomous, team-based automation is already being developed, it is important to acknowledge the current hurdles. The effectiveness of such multi-agent systems is presently constrained by the reasoning limitations of LLMs they are using. Furthermore, their ability to genuinely learn from one another and improve as a cohesive unit is still in its early stages. Overcoming these technological bottlenecks is the critical next step, and doing so will unlock the profound promise of this level: the ability to automate entire business workflows from start to finish.

尽管这种自主的、团队式自动化的愿景已经在研发之中，但我们必须正视当前的障碍。这类多智能体系统的有效性，目前仍受限于它们所使用的 LLM 的推理能力。此外，它们作为一个凝聚整体真正相互学习、共同进步的能力，还处在早期阶段。攻克这些技术瓶颈是关键的下一步；而一旦做到，将释放这一层级的深远承诺：端到端地自动化整条业务工作流的能力。

The Future of Agents: Top Five Hypotheses智能体的未来：五大假设

Hypothesis 1: The Emergence of the Generalist Agent假设一：通用型智能体的出现

The first hypothesis is that AI agents will evolve from narrow specialists into true generalists capable of managing complex, ambiguous, and long-term goals with high reliability. For instance, you could give an agent a simple

第一个假设是：AI 智能体将从狭窄的专才，演进为真正的通才——能够以高可靠性管理复杂、模糊、长期的目标。例如，你可以给智能体一个简单的

— 原书第 16 页 —

prompt like “Plan my company’s offsite retreat for 30 people in Lisbon next quarter.” The agent would then manage the entire project for weeks, handling everything from budget approvals and flight negotiations to venue selection and creating a detailed itinerary from employee feedback, all while providing regular updates. Achieving this level of autonomy will require fundamental breakthroughs in AI reasoning, memory, and near-perfect reliability. An alternative, yet not mutually exclusive, approach is the rise of small language models (SLMs). This “Lego-like” concept involves composing systems from small, specialized expert agents rather than scaling up a single monolithic model. This method promises systems that are cheaper, faster to debug, and easier to deploy. Ultimately, the development of large generalist models and the composition of smaller specialized ones are both plausible paths forward, and they could even complement each other.

提示词：“帮我公司规划下季度在里斯本举办的 30 人异地团建。” 智能体随后会连续几周管理整个项目，从预算审批、机票谈判，到场地选择、根据员工反馈制定详细行程，样样包办，并定期汇报进展。要达到这种自主程度，需要在 AI 推理、记忆以及近乎完美的可靠性上取得根本性突破。另一条与之并不互斥的路径，是小语言模型（SLM）的兴起。这种“乐高式”思路，是用小型、专门的专家智能体拼装出系统，而不是把单一的铁板模型越做越大。这种方法有望带来更便宜、调试更快、部署更容易的系统。归根结底，研发大型通用模型与拼装小型专门模型，都是可行的前进路径，二者甚至可以互补。

Hypothesis 2: Deep Personalization and Proactive Goal Discovery假设二：深度个性化与主动式目标发现

The second hypothesis posits that agents will become deeply personalized and proactive partners. We are witnessing the emergence of a new class of agent: the proactive partner. By learning from your unique patterns and goals, these systems are beginning to shift from just following orders to anticipating your needs. AI systems operate as agents when they move beyond simply responding to chats or instructions. They initiate and execute tasks on behalf of the user, actively collaborating in the process. This moves beyond simple task execution into the realm of proactive goal discovery.

第二个假设认为，智能体将成为深度个性化、主动出击的伙伴。我们正在见证一类新智能体的诞生：主动伙伴。通过学习你独特的行为模式与目标，这些系统开始从“只听命行事”转向“预判你的需求”。当 AI 系统不再只是回应聊天或指令，而是代表用户主动发起并执行任务、在过程中积极协作时，它们就以智能体的方式运作了。这超越了简单的任务执行，进入了主动式目标发现的疆域。

For instance, if you are exploring sustainable energy, the agent might identify your latent goal and proactively support it by suggesting courses or summarizing research. While these systems are still developing, their trajectory is clear. They will become increasingly proactive, learning to take initiative on your behalf when highly confident that the action will be helpful. Ultimately, the agent becomes an indispensable ally, helping you discover and achieve ambitions you have yet to fully articulate.

例如，如果你正在探索可持续能源，智能体可能识别出你潜在的目标，并通过推荐课程或综述研究来主动支持它。尽管这些系统仍在发展中，其轨迹却已清晰：它们会变得越来越主动，当高度确信某个行动会对你有益时，就学着替你主动出手。最终，智能体会成为一位不可或缺的盟友，帮你发现并实现那些你尚未充分言明的抱负。

Hypothesis 3: Embodiment and Physical World Interaction假设三：具身性与物理世界交互

This hypothesis foresees agents breaking free from their purely digital confines to operate in the physical world. By integrating agentic AI with robotics, we will see the rise of “embodied agents.” Instead of just booking a handyman, you might ask your home agent to fix a leaky tap. The agent would use its

这个假设预见智能体挣脱纯数字的牢笼，到物理世界中运作。通过把智能体式 AI 与机器人技术结合，我们将看到“具身智能体”的兴起。你不再只是预约一位水暖工，而可能直接让你的家庭智能体去修理漏水的水龙头。智能体会用它的

— 原书第 17 页 —

vision sensors to perceive the problem, access a library of plumbing knowledge to formulate a plan, and then control its robotic manipulators with precision to perform the repair. This would represent a monumental step, bridging the gap between digital intelligence and physical action and transforming everything from manufacturing and logistics to elder care and home maintenance.

视觉传感器去感知问题，调用一个水暖知识库来制定方案，再精准控制它的机械臂完成维修。这将是具有里程碑意义的一步，弥合数字智能与物理行动之间的鸿沟，重塑从制造、物流到养老看护、家庭维护的方方面面。

Hypothesis 4: The Agent-Driven Economy假设四：智能体驱动的经济

The fourth hypothesis is that highly autonomous agents will become active participants in the economy, creating new markets and business models. We could see agents acting as independent economic entities, tasked with maximizing a specific outcome, such as profit. An entrepreneur could launch an agent to run an entire e-commerce business. The agent would identify trending products by analyzing social media, generate marketing copy and visuals, manage supply chain logistics by interacting with other automated systems, and dynamically adjust pricing based on real-time demand. This shift would create a new, hyper-efficient “agent economy” operating at a speed and scale impossible for humans to manage directly.

第四个假设是：高度自主的智能体将成为经济中的活跃参与者，创造新的市场与商业模式。我们可能看到智能体作为独立的经济实体行动，被指派去最大化某个特定结果，比如利润。一位创业者可以启动一个智能体来运营一整个电商生意：它通过分析社交媒体识别爆款商品，生成营销文案与视觉素材，通过与其他自动化系统交互来管理供应链物流，并根据实时需求动态调价。这一转变将催生一个全新的、超高效率的“智能体经济”，其运转速度与规模是人类无法直接管理的。

Hypothesis 5: The Goal-Driven, Metamorphic Multi-Agent System假设五：目标驱动的、可蜕变的多智能体系统

This hypothesis posits the emergence of intelligent systems that operate not from explicit programming, but from a declared goal. The user simply states the desired outcome, and the system autonomously figures out how to achieve it. This marks a fundamental shift towards metamorphic multi-agent systems capable of true self-improvement at both the individual and collective levels.

这个假设提出：将出现这样一类智能系统——它们不是基于显式编程、而是基于一个被声明的目标来运作。用户只需陈述期望的结果，系统便自主琢磨如何实现它。这标志着向“可蜕变多智能体系统”的根本转变，这类系统能够在个体与集体两个层面上实现真正的自我改进。

This system would be a dynamic entity, not a single agent. It would have the ability to analyze its own performance and modify the topology of its multi-agent workforce, creating, duplicating, or removing agents as needed to form the most effective team for the task at hand. This evolution happens at multiple levels:

这个系统将是一个动态实体，而非单个智能体。它将有能力分析自身表现，并修改其多智能体劳动力的拓扑结构——按需创建、复制或移除智能体，为手头任务组建最有效的团队。这种蜕变发生在多个层面：

  • Architectural modification: At the deepest level, individual agents can rewrite their own source code and re-architect their internal structures for higher efficiency, as in the original hypothesis.架构层修改：在最深层，单个智能体可以重写自己的源代码、重新架构其内部结构以获得更高效率，正如最初的假设所述。
— 原书第 18 页 —
  • Instructional modification: At a higher level, the system continuously performs automatic prompt engineering and context engineering. It refines the instructions and information given to each agent, ensuring that they are operating with optimal guidance without any human intervention.指令层修改：在更高层，系统持续自动进行提示工程与上下文工程。它精修给每个智能体的指令与信息，确保它们在无需任何人工干预的情况下获得最优指导。

For instance, an entrepreneur would simply declare the intent: “Launch a successful e-commerce business selling artisanal coffee.” The system, without further programming, would spring into action. It might initially spawn a “Market Research” agent and a “Branding” agent. Based on the initial findings, it could decide to remove the branding agent and spawn three new specialized agents: a “Logo Design” agent, a “Webstore Platform” agent, and a “Supply Chain” agent. It would constantly tune their internal prompts for better performance. If the webstore agent becomes a bottleneck, the system might duplicate it into three parallel agents to work on different parts of the site, effectively re-architecting its own structure on the fly to best achieve the declared goal.

例如，一位创业者只需声明意图：“开一家卖手工咖啡、生意成功的电商。” 系统无需进一步编程，便立刻行动起来。它最初可能会派出一个“市场调研”智能体和一个“品牌”智能体。基于初步发现，它可能决定撤掉品牌智能体，再派出三个新的专门智能体：一个“标志设计”智能体、一个“网店平台”智能体、一个“供应链”智能体。它会持续调优它们的内部提示词以获得更好表现。如果网店智能体成了瓶颈，系统可能把它复制成三个并行智能体，分头处理网站的不同部分——实际上就是在运行时重新架构自身结构，以最佳地实现所声明的目标。

Conclusion小结

In essence, an AI agent represents a significant leap from traditional models, functioning as an autonomous system that perceives, plans, and acts to achieve specific goals. The evolution of this technology is advancing from single-tool-using agents to complex, collaborative multi-agent systems that tackle multifaceted objectives. Future hypotheses predict the emergence of generalist, personalized, and even physically embodied agents that will become active participants in the economy. This ongoing development signals a major paradigm shift towards self-improving, goal-driven systems poised to automate entire workflows and fundamentally redefine our relationship with technology.

本质上，AI 智能体代表着相对于传统模型的一次重大飞跃：它作为一个自主系统，感知、规划并行动以实现特定目标。这项技术的演进，正从使用单一工具的智能体，迈向处理多面目标的复杂、协作式多智能体系统。未来的种种假设预言：通用型、个性化、乃至物理具身的智能体将会出现，并成为经济中的活跃参与者。这场持续演进，标志着一场重大的范式转移——转向自我改进、目标驱动的系统，它们蓄势待发，将自动化整条工作流，并从根本上重新定义我们与技术的关系。

Preface作者序

Welcome to Agentic Design Patterns: A Hands-On Guide to Building Intelligent Systems. As we look across the landscape of modern artificial intelligence, we see a clear evolution from simple, reactive programs to sophisticated, autonomous entities capable of understanding context, making decisions, and interacting dynamically with their environment and other systems. These are the intelligent agents and the agentic systems they comprise.

欢迎阅读《Agentic Design Patterns: A Hands-On Guide to Building Intelligent Systems》。纵览现代人工智能的版图，我们看到一条清晰的演进轨迹：从简单、反应式的程序，到能够理解上下文、做出决策、并与环境及其他系统动态交互的复杂、自主的实体。这些就是智能体，以及由它们构成的智能体系统。

The advent of powerful large language models (LLMs) has provided unprecedented capabilities for understanding and generating humanlike content such as text and media, serving as the cognitive engine for many of these agents. However, orchestrating these capabilities into systems that can reliably achieve complex goals requires more than just a powerful model. It requires structure, design, and a thoughtful approach to how the agent perceives, plans, acts, and interacts.

强大的大语言模型（LLM）的问世，为理解和生成文本、媒体等类人内容提供了前所未有的能力，充当着其中许多智能体的认知引擎。然而，要把这些能力编排成能够可靠实现复杂目标的系统，光有一个强大模型还不够。它还需要结构、设计，以及一套关于智能体如何感知、规划、行动与交互的深思熟虑的方法。

Think of building intelligent systems as creating a complex work of art or engineering on a canvas. This canvas is not a blank visual space, but rather the underlying infrastructure and frameworks that provide the environment and tools for your agents to exist and operate. It is the foundation upon which you will build your intelligent application, managing state, communication, tool access, and flow of logic.

不妨把构建智能系统想象成在一块画布上创作一件复杂的艺术品或工程作品。这块画布不是一块空白的视觉空间，而是底层的基础设施与框架，为你的智能体提供存在与运作的环境和工具。它是你构建智能应用的地基，负责管理状态、通信、工具访问和逻辑流转。

Building effectively on this agentic canvas demands more than just throwing components together. It requires understanding proven techniques—patterns—that address common challenges in designing and implementing agent behavior. Just as architectural patterns guide the construction of a building, or design patterns structure software, agentic design patterns provide reusable solutions for the recurring problems you will face when bringing intelligent agents to life on your chosen canvas.

要在这块智能体画布上高效地构建，光把组件胡乱拼凑在一起是不够的。它要求你理解那些经过验证的技术——模式——它们应对的是设计与实现智能体行为时的常见挑战。正如建筑模式指导一座建筑的营造、设计模式为软件赋予结构一样，智能体设计模式为你在所选画布上把智能体变为现实时反复遇到的问题，提供可复用的解决方案。

— 原书第 21 页 —

What Are Agentic Systems?什么是智能体系统？

At its core, an agentic system is a computational entity designed to perceive its environment (both digital and potentially physical), make informed decisions based on those perceptions and a set of predefined or learned goals, and execute actions to achieve those goals autonomously. Unlike traditional software, which follows rigid, step-by-step instructions, agents exhibit a degree of flexibility and initiative.

从本质上说，智能体系统是一个计算实体：它被设计为感知所处环境（既包括数字环境，也可能包括物理环境），基于这些感知以及一组预定义或习得的目标做出有依据的决策，并自主执行动作以达成这些目标。与遵循死板、按部就班指令的传统软件不同，智能体表现出一定程度的灵活性与主动性。

Imagine you need a system to manage customer inquiries. A traditional system might follow a fixed script. An agentic system, however, could perceive the nuances of a customer’s query, access knowledge bases, interact with other internal systems (like order management), potentially ask clarifying questions, and proactively resolve the issue, perhaps even anticipating future needs. These agents operate on the canvas of your application’s infrastructure, utilizing the services and data available to them.

设想你需要一个系统来处理客户咨询。传统系统可能照本宣科地走一套固定脚本；而一个智能体系统则能感知客户查询中的细微差别、访问知识库、与其他内部系统（如订单管理）交互、可能提出澄清性问题，并主动解决问题，甚至预判未来的需求。这些智能体在你应用基础设施的画布上运作，利用它们可用的服务与数据。

Agentic systems are often characterized by features like autonomy, allowing them to act without constant human oversight; proactiveness, initiating actions towards their goals; and reactiveness, responding effectively to changes in their environment. They are fundamentally goal oriented, constantly working towards objectives. A critical capability is tool use, enabling them to interact with external APIs, databases, or services: effectively reaching out beyond their immediate canvas. They possess memory, retain information across interactions, and can engage in communication with users, other systems, or even other agents operating on the same or connected canvases.

智能体系统通常具备这样一些特征：自主性（autonomy），使其无需持续人工监督即可行动；主动性（proactiveness），面向目标发起动作；反应性（reactiveness），对环境变化做出有效响应。它们从根本上是目标导向的，始终朝目标推进。一项关键能力是工具使用（tool use），使其能够与外部 API、数据库或服务交互——有效地把触角伸到自己紧邻画布之外。它们拥有记忆，在多次交互之间保留信息，并能与用户、其他系统、乃至运行在同一块或相连画布上的其他智能体进行通信。

Effectively realizing these characteristics introduces significant complexity. How does the agent maintain state across multiple steps on its canvas? How does it decide when and how to use a tool? How is communication between different agents managed? How do you build resilience into the system to handle unexpected outcomes or errors?

要真正实现这些特性，会引入相当大的复杂度。智能体如何在画布上跨多个步骤维护状态？它如何决定何时以及如何使用工具？不同智能体之间的通信如何管理？你又如何在系统中构建韧性，以应对意料之外的结果或错误？

Why Patterns Matter in Agent Development为什么模式在智能体开发中如此重要

This complexity is precisely why agentic design patterns are indispensable. They are not rigid rules, but rather battle-tested templates or blueprints that offer proven approaches to standard design and implementation challenges in the agentic domain. By recognizing and applying these design patterns, you gain access to solutions that enhance the structure, maintainability, reliability, and efficiency of the agents you build on your canvas.

这种复杂度，正是智能体设计模式不可或缺的原因。它们不是死板的规则，而是久经沙场的模板或蓝图，为智能体领域中常见的设计与实现挑战提供经过验证的方法。通过识别并应用这些设计模式，你便能获得那些能提升你在画布上所建智能体的结构、可维护性、可靠性与效率的解决方案。

— 原书第 22 页 —

Using design patterns helps you avoid reinventing fundamental solutions for tasks like managing conversational flow, integrating external capabilities, or coordinating multiple agent actions. They provide a common language and structure that makes your agent’s logic clearer and easier for others (and yourself in the future) to understand and maintain. Implementing patterns designed for error handling or state management directly contributes to building more robust and reliable systems. Leveraging these established approaches accelerates your development process, allowing you to focus on the unique aspects of your application rather than the foundational mechanics of agent behavior.

使用设计模式，能帮你避免在管理对话流、集成外部能力或协调多个智能体动作等任务上重复造轮子。它们提供一套共同语言与结构，让你的智能体逻辑更清晰，也让别人（以及未来的你自己）更容易理解和维护。实现那些专为错误处理或状态管理设计的模式，会直接助力你构建更健壮、更可靠的系统。借助这些既定方法，你能加速开发进程，把精力放在应用的独特之处，而不是智能体行为的底层机制上。

This book extracts 21 key design patterns that represent fundamental building blocks and techniques for constructing sophisticated agents on various technical canvases. Understanding and applying these patterns will significantly elevate your ability to design and implement intelligent systems effectively.

本书提炼了 21 个关键设计模式，它们代表着在各种技术画布上构建复杂智能体的基本构件与技术。理解并应用这些模式，将显著提升你有效设计与实现智能系统的能力。

Overview of the Book and How to Use It本书概览与使用方法

This book, Agentic Design Patterns: A Hands-On Guide to Building Intelligent Systems, is crafted to be a practical and accessible resource. Its primary focus is on clearly explaining each agentic pattern and providing concrete, runnable code examples to demonstrate its implementation. Across 21 dedicated chapters, we will explore a diverse range of design patterns, from foundational concepts like structuring sequential operations (prompt chaining) and external interaction (tool use) to more advanced topics like collaborative work (multi-agent collaboration) and self-improvement (self-correction).

本书《Agentic Design Patterns: A Hands-On Guide to Building Intelligent Systems》被打造为一本实用、易读的资源。它的核心关注点，是清晰地讲解每一种智能体模式，并给出具体、可运行的代码示例来演示其实现。在 21 个专门章节中，我们将探索一系列丰富的设计模式：从组织顺序操作（提示链）、外部交互（工具调用）等基础概念，到协作式工作（多智能体协作）、自我改进（自我纠错）等更高级的主题。

The book is organized chapter by chapter, with each chapter delving into a single agentic pattern. Within each chapter, you will find:

本书按章组织，每一章深入一种智能体模式。在每一章里，你会看到：

  • A detailed Pattern Overview providing a clear explanation of the pattern and its role in agentic design.详细的“模式概述”，清晰解释该模式及其在智能体设计中的作用。
  • A section on Practical Applications and Use Cases illustrating real-world scenarios where the pattern is invaluable and the benefits it brings.“实践应用与用例”一节，展示该模式大显身手的真实场景及其带来的收益。
  • A Hands-On Code Example offering practical, runnable code that demonstrates the pattern’s implementation using prominent agent development frameworks. This is where you will see how to apply the pattern within the context of a technical canvas.“动手实践代码示例”，用主流智能体开发框架给出可运行的实际代码，演示该模式的实现；在这里你将看到如何在某个技术画布的语境中应用该模式。
— 原书第 23 页 —
  • Key Takeaways summarizing the most crucial points for a quick review.“要点回顾”，总结最关键的内容以便快速复习。
  • References for further exploration, providing resources for deeper learning on the pattern and related concepts.“参考文献”，提供就该模式及相关概念深入学习的资源。

While the chapters are ordered to build concepts progressively, feel free to use the book as a reference, jumping to chapters that address specific challenges you face in your own agent development projects. The appendices provide a comprehensive look at advanced prompting techniques, principles for applying AI agents in real-world environments, and an overview of essential agentic frameworks. To complement this, practical online-only tutorials are included, offering step-by-step guidance on building agents with specific platforms like Agentspace and for the command-line interface. The emphasis throughout is on practical application; we strongly encourage you to run the code examples, experiment with them, and adapt them to build your own intelligent systems on your chosen canvas.

虽然各章按循序渐进、逐步建立概念的顺序排列，但你完全可以把本书当作案头参考书，直接跳到那些解决你自己智能体开发项目中具体挑战的章节。附录全面介绍了高级提示技术、在真实环境中应用 AI 智能体的原则，以及主流智能体框架概览。作为补充，本书还配有仅供在线阅读的实践教程，手把手指导你用 Agentspace 等特定平台以及命令行界面构建智能体。全书的重点始终放在实践应用上；我们强烈建议你亲手运行代码示例、动手实验，并把它们改造适配，在你所选的画布上构建自己的智能系统。

A great question I hear is, “With AI changing so fast, why write a book that could be quickly outdated?” My motivation was actually the opposite. It is precisely because things are moving so quickly that we need to step back and identify the underlying principles that are solidifying. Patterns like RAG, reflection, routing, memory, and the others I discuss are becoming fundamental building blocks. This book is an invitation to reflect on these core ideas, which provide the foundation we need to build upon. Humans need these reflection moments on foundation patterns.

我常听到一个好问题：“AI 变化这么快，为什么还要写一本可能很快过时的书？” 我的动机恰恰相反。正因为变化如此之快，我们才更需要退一步，去识别那些正在沉淀下来的底层原则。RAG、反思、路由、记忆等我讨论的模式，正在成为基本构件。本书邀请你一同反思这些核心理念，它们为我们提供了赖以构建的地基。人类需要在基础模式上有这样停下来反思的时刻。

Introduction to the Frameworks Used所用框架简介

To provide a tangible “canvas” for our code examples (see also Part II), we will primarily utilize three prominent agent development frameworks. LangChain, along with its stateful extension LangGraph, provides a flexible way to chain together language models and other components, offering a robust canvas for building complex sequences and graphs of operations. Crew AI provides a structured framework specifically designed for orchestrating multiple AI agents, roles, and tasks, acting as a canvas particularly well suited for collaborative agent systems. The Google Agent Developer Kit (Google ADK) offers tools and components for building, evaluating, and deploying agents, providing another valuable canvas, often integrated with Google’s AI infrastructure.

为了给我们的代码示例提供一块触手可及的“画布”（另见第二部分），我们将主要使用三个主流智能体开发框架。LangChain 连同其带状态的扩展 LangGraph，提供了一种把语言模型和其他组件串接起来的灵活方式，为构建复杂的操作序列与图提供了一块健壮的画布。Crew AI 提供了一个专门为编排多个 AI 智能体、角色与任务而设计的结构化框架，是一块特别适合协作式智能体系统的画布。Google 智能体开发套件（Google ADK）提供用于构建、评估和部署智能体的工具与组件，是另一块有价值的画布，且常与 Google 的 AI 基础设施集成。

These frameworks represent different facets of the agent development canvas, each with its strengths. By showing examples across these tools, you will

这些框架代表着智能体开发画布的不同侧面，各有所长。通过在这些工具上展示示例，你将

— 原书第 24 页 —

gain a broader understanding of how the patterns can be applied regardless of the specific technical environment you choose for your agentic systems. The examples are designed to clearly illustrate the pattern’s core logic and its implementation on the framework’s canvas, focusing on clarity and practicality.

更广泛地理解：无论你为自己的智能体系统选择哪种具体技术环境，这些模式都能加以应用。示例的设计力求清晰展示模式的核心逻辑及其在该框架画布上的实现，聚焦于清晰性与实用性。

By the end of this book, you will not only understand the fundamental concepts behind 21 essential agentic patterns but also possess the practical knowledge and code examples to apply them effectively, enabling you to build more intelligent, capable, and autonomous systems on your chosen development canvas. Let us begin this hands-on journey!

读完本书，你不仅会理解 21 个必备智能体模式背后的基本概念，还将掌握有效应用它们的实践知识与代码示例，从而在你所选的开发画布上构建更智能、更强大、更自主的系统。让我们开始这场动手之旅吧！

Zürich, Switzerland · Antonio Gullí
